## 1. THE CLAIMS (register-tagged, with timestamps)

**C1 — Architecture: parallel modular unconscious processors + a narrow, capacity-limited central workspace. [QUOTE,L97-111 · 03:46–04:31]**
*"like any complex machine the brain contains a variety of specialized processes that all operate unconsciously and in a modular manner in parallel with each other… consciousness is an evolved solution to a computational problem which is the need to be able to extract information relevant to the organism['s] goals from any of these processors… and make it available for further reflection. Detach it from where it came from. Detach it from the time where it came from. Make it available for long-term reflection."*

**C2 — THE IDENTITY CLAIM (the load-bearing over-reach): phenomenal = access. [QUOTE,L130-138 · 04:58–05:22]**
*"what we subjectively experience as being conscious of X is just the global availability [of] information. So I don't disagree that there are phenomenal states. I'm not sure I like the term but we experience things but what we experience is what we access… I think there is no distinction … between what we experience and what we have access."*
→ Dehaene **collapses** the phenomenal/access distinction (he does not inflate access into a phenomenal claim — he denies the second category exists). Tagged [ATTACK SURFACE] as a *definitional* move (see §5).

**C3 — Definition of ignition. [QUOTE,L88-90 · 03:22–03:33]**
*"this is what I call ignition where you have a nonlinear phenomenon, all or none — you access the information or you don't — and it reflects the global integration of the attended signal into an internal model."*

**C4 — Ignition = metastable broadcast. [QUOTE,L263-268 · 09:50–10:03]**
*"the trace of consciousness is the global ignition of the system. And by this we mean a metastable activity for about 100–200 millisecond minimum which can broadcast and synchronize the processors."*

**C5 — Completeness claim (GNW's strongest positive assertion). [QUOTE,L271-274 · 10:07–10:18]**
*"one key idea is that this ignition should contain a complete neural code for the current subjective contents of consciousness… whatever we are conscious of it should be decodable."*

**C6 — The workspace is distributed, not prefrontal-only; content = an activity vector. [QUOTE,L148-160 · 05:27–06:18]**
*"a central system of high level areas… the sudden activation of a subset of neurons with long-dist[ance] axons… they have to be distributed. Not a single neuron can do the job… It's not a single neuron that has the concept. It's a pattern of activity, a vector of activity that has the conscious content."*

**C7 — Functionalism / substrate independence. [QUOTE,L207-220 · 07:45–08:20]**
*"For me the global neural workspace is a functionalist computational theory… different implementation is possible, that machine consciousness is possible with a non-biological implementation. What matters is the style of computation."*

**C8 — Negative markers: what does NOT ignite. [QUOTE,L351-355 · 13:23–13:34]**
*"the so-called N1-170 … can be very strongly activated for stimuli that the subject reports not seeing. [That] means that this early activation is not a correlate of consciousness."*
And **[QUOTE,L552-560 · 21:17–21:30]:** *"you can have exactly the same level of activation in V4 on conscious and unconscious trials… therefore [it is] not a marker of consciousness."* → early sensory amplitude is not consciousness; only the late, self-sustained activation is.

**C9 — Masking threshold as the hard boundary. [near L440 · 17:09–17:21]**
Below ~50 ms the signal is a *"feed-forward"* cascade that *"never create[s] a stable representation"*; above it *"there's a crossing of a threshold and you have more stability, meta-stability."*

**C10 — The false-alarm finding. [QUOTE,L462-468 & L563-572 · 17:48–18:07, 21:44–22:02]**
*"a self-sustained recurrent representation that is able to sustain itself… only on the trials that [subjects] report seeing — and that includes the blue curve with the false alarms. If the monkey makes a false alarm, you get also activation in the system as if he had seen some stimulus or believes he has seen a stimulus or committed to reporting seeing a stimulus."*
→ The marker tracks the **report/commitment**, not the stimulus. **This is our provenance≠truth claim, measured on an electrode.**

**C11 — Cross-species. [QUOTE,L486-489 & L753-758 · 18:32–18:36, 29:12–29:33]**
Monkeys (with Peter Roelfsema; minimal dot of light at varying luminance) show the same transient→sustained transition; crows show *"exactly the same transition — initial representation of stimulus intensity, late representation of the subjective report"* (Nieder Science paper); infants show a *"fully all-or-none uh late negativity"* against a *"fully graded representation of the duration of the stimulus"* (the baby/seal-cub no-report work). *"Ignition is just one of these signatures that we share."* Lineages separated by ~300 My.

**C12 — The no-report amendment (self-correction, credit to the source). [QUOTE,L1452-1458 · 55:56–56:35]**
*"essentially all that I said … remains under [a] no report situation except for the P300 waveform of the event related potentials — so in that respect my book should be updated."*

**C13 — Consciousness ≠ attention. [QUOTE,L167-172 · 06:24–06:45]**
Attention can operate non-consciously; *"conscious access corresponds to the last stage of selection."* Consciousness is **untied from stimulus timing** (it can hold a 100-ms flash arbitrarily long).

**C14 — Clinical external validity. [near L820-830 · 29:43–30:04]**
The markers are used (with Lionel Naccache's clinic) *"to predict whether the person is still conscious or … whether he's going to recover consciousness"* in disorders of consciousness.

|---|------|----------|-------------------------------|---------|

GNW adds that the workspace is *distributed* (parietal+prefrontal, not prefrontal-only), which *refines* canon's "prefrontal GUI." |
| 2 | **Threshold / non-linearity** | All-or-none ignition; ~50 ms mask threshold; metastable 100–200 ms; P3 non-linearity; single-trial report-sorted | "Filter" gates GPU→GUI | **(b) DIFFER — GNW BETTER.** GNW gives a *quantitative* threshold + a *non-linearity signature*. Canon foregrounds the subtraction; GNW foregrounds the distribution. Not different mechanisms — different metaphors over one mechanism. |

| 5 | **What it PREDICTS** | Threshold, non-linearity, marker location (late self-sustained prefrontal), report-locked false alarms, cross-species invariance | Filter can be bypassed (ketamine/dreams); GPU runs with GUI off; GUI↔GPU divergence | **(a/b) MIXED.** The *bypass* prediction is canon-only and GNW-silent — but note GNW's own architecture entails it (unconscious parallel processors *already* run without ignition). So the "bypass" is not a novelty; it is a *consequence* of GNW too. |

This **constrains canon**: we cannot *equate* consciousness with report/GUI, because Dehaene's own data show the signature is report-independent (the P300 caveat is the one exception). |

**Honest synthesis (§2 verdict).** On the axis that matters — *is the architecture the same?* — **yes, GNW and our GPU/GUI are the same claim in two vocabularies, and GNW is the better-formalized version of it.** The "internal filter" is closest to GNW-with-worse-formalism: GNW specifies the threshold, the non-linearity, the marker location, and a positive completeness claim that our filter does not. The **one genuine, nameable difference is the FUNCTION assigned to the workspace**: GNW says the workspace exists to *liberate* information from its source module and its moment of origin for flexible, detached, long-term reuse (C1 — "detach it from where it came from… from the time where it came from"); canon says consciousness is a *filter* that excludes (subtraction/gating). **These are opposite framings of the same mechanism** — but they are *not* the same *claim about what the mechanism is for*. GNW's positive, constructive, completeness-and-broadcast framing is stronger and better-evidenced than canon's subtractive filter framing. **Recommended canon action: stop claiming novelty for the GPU/GUI split against GNW; adopt GNW's threshold/non-linearity as canon's formalism, and retain only the ledger/commit extension (§4, row 6) as the candidate differentiator.**

## 4. PRE-REGISTERED FALSIFIERS

- **F-GNW1 (novelty — meta-falsifier).** *Falsified:* if GNW's formalism reproduces every prediction canon makes about the GUI, canon's novelty claim against GNW is dead. *Test:* map canon's GUI predictions to GNW 1:1; any canon prediction **not** entailed by GNW is the only defensible novelty. *Prior:* §2 suggests the map is near-total.
- **F-GNW2 (multi-content).** *Falsifies GNW's discrete-ignition core:* if 3–4 simultaneously reported contents produce **multiple simultaneous ignitions** rather than one or fast-switched ones. *Supports GNW:* a single ignition persists under multi-content load. Addresses F7.
- **F-GNW3 (completeness).** *Falsifies GNW's positive claim (C5):* if single-trial decoders cannot recover the reported content from the ignition vector above chance on held-out trials. If it fails, canon's subtractive filter is the more defensible description, and GNW's advantage (§2 row 9) evaporates.
- **F-GNW4 (report-independence).** *Falsifies the access-identification:* a no-report paradigm in which the ignition signature is *absent* while the content is still behaviorally used. *Constrains canon:* a report-free signature present in the absence of any commit would pressure canon's "access = commit."
- **F-GNW5 (scope / exceedance).** *Tests the §3-F3 candidate exceedance:* a system that holds a committed content, re-addresses it across sessions (ledger), with **no within-window ignition** would show a phenomenon GNW does not cover. If ignition is always required for later address, F3 collapses into GNW.
- **F-GNW6 (commitment direction).** *Discriminates correlation from commitment:* if ignition on false alarms systematically **precedes and causes** the report, that favours an active commitment interpretation over a passive correlate — the stronger form of C10.

## 5. HARD-PROBLEM POSTURE & ATTACK SURFACES

**GNW is a theory of ACCESS consciousness, offered as a theory of consciousness full stop by collapsing the distinction (C2).** Dehaene does **not** over-reach *upward* from access to phenomenal — there is no moment in the talk where he claims the ignition *creates* or *explains* phenomenal experience. He does the opposite: he **denies the phenomenal category is distinct** (*"what we experience is what we access… there is no distinction"*, L132-138) and rejects a pictorial phenomenal reading of the oscillation data (*"I don't want to suggest there's a kind of qualia-like cloud that comes from the oscillations"*, L2104-2107 · 81:50–81:56).

- **[ATTACK SURFACE] (definitional, not empirical).** The Hoffmann/Chalmers-style critique lands *precisely* here: GNW does not **solve** the hard problem, it **dissolves it by stipulation**. That is a legitimate research strategy but it is not an empirical result, and C2's identity claim ("experience = access") is asserted, not derived. Canon should quote C2 as a *stance*, never as a *finding*.
- **No [ATTACK SURFACE] for empirical over-reach.** To his credit, Dehaene flags his own limits: the P300 no-report exception ("my book should be updated", C12), and the open question whether working memory is *entirely* conscious (§ near L2140). He is unusually self-limiting.
- **[ATTACK SURFACE] on OUR OWN prior file.** The Bolonkin note's "LLMs including Claude" line is **not in the transcript**. Flag it, do not propagate it. (File left unmodified per read-only constraint.)

## 6. ★ SINGLE STRONGEST [CRITICAL DIVERGENCE] AGAINST CANON

> **GNW's workspace is a COMPLETENESS + DETACHMENT device; canon's "filter" is a SUBTRACTION device. These are opposite functional claims about the same mechanism, and GNW's is the better-evidenced one.**

GNW says the workspace's job is *positive*: to hold a **complete, decodable neural code** for the current content (C5) and **liberate it from its source module and moment of origin** so it can be reused flexibly and long (C1). Canon says the job is *negative*: to **filter** — to exclude the unattended/unfit. On GNW's evidence, consciousness is **not primarily a gate against noise**; it is a mechanism of **temporal and modular detachment and global re-use**. If GNW is right, canon's central metaphor **mislocates the function of the very thing it is a theory of**, and canon's "internal filter between GPU and GUI" is best understood as **GNW with worse formalism and an inverted function-claim.** Canon must either produce a prediction that a pure filter makes and a completeness/broadcast workspace does not (F-GNW1 → likely empty), or concede the framing and keep only the ledger/commit scope-extension (F3).

**Calibrated verdict:** GNW and canon's GPU/GUI are, on the architecture axis, **[VERIFIED]-level the same claim in two vocabularies** — GNW is the mainstream formalization of what canon asserts informally. The "internal filter" is **GNW minus its threshold, minus its non-linearity, minus its completeness claim, and with a subtraction framing where GNW has a liberation framing.** The only candidate genuine differences are (i) canon's ledger/commit scope-extension (F3, likely a scope difference, not a rival theory) and (ii) a small exceedance on multi-content (F7/F-GNW2) that JSpace partially answers. Canon's net position: **the GPU/GUI split is not novel against GNW; canon's defensible residue is the ledger/commit claim and the JSpace causal handle — not the split itself.**
